mechanism_narrative: Persistent negative WORKPLACES mobility (declining from +1.3 to -1.7 over four weeks) signals sustained work-from-home adoption. This reduces commuter foot traffic and suppresses retail visitation, driving RETAIL_REC further negative over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES declined monotonically from +1.3 to -1.7 over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over the next 28 days exceeds the mean over the last 28 days, or WORKPLACES reverses to positive territory within two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: Sustained elevated RESIDENTIAL mobility (+7.3 to +7.9) combined with depressed RETAIL_REC (-13.9) indicates consumers are sheltering in place and substituting home-based activities for retail visits. This behavioral lock-in persists, keeping RETAIL_REC suppressed over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL stable at +7.3 to +7.9 across all four weeks
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL mobility falls below +5.0 for two consecutive weeks, or RETAIL_REC rises above -10.0 while RESIDENTIAL remains above +7.0.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility has declined monotonically from -9.9 to -11.1 over four weeks, signaling reduced public transport usage and commuting. When TRANSIT falls below -11.0, retail accessibility declines sharply, triggering a threshold effect that suppresses RETAIL_REC further in the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -11.0 for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT at -11.1 in t-0w, lowest in series
failure_condition: TRANSIT rebounds above -10.0 within one week, or RETAIL_REC rises above -12.0 despite TRANSIT remaining below -11.0.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility remains deeply negative (-38.0 to -43.1), indicating outdoor recreation is severely constrained by seasonal or policy factors. This constraint extends to retail-and-recreation venues, which are often co-located or psychologically bundled with parks. The suppression persists over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS consistently below -38.0 across all four weeks
failure_condition: PARKS mobility rises above -30.0 within two weeks, or RETAIL_REC rises above -10.0 while PARKS remains below -35.0.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility remains stable and elevated (+9.6 to +10.4), indicating consumers prioritize essential shopping. When essential shopping is high and RETAIL_REC is low, consumers exhibit a bifurcated behavior: they visit pharmacies and grocers but avoid discretionary retail. This bifurcation persists, keeping RETAIL_REC suppressed over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM above +9.0 AND RETAIL_REC below -13.0 simultaneously
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM stable at +9.6 to +10.4, RETAIL_REC stable at -13.3 to -13.9
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above -12.0 while GROCERY_PHARM remains above +9.0, or GROCERY_PHARM falls below +8.0 for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: The combination of declining WORKPLACES (-1.7), declining TRANSIT (-11.1), and suppressed RETAIL_REC (-13.9) suggests a tightening policy regime restricting mobility. When TRANSIT falls more than 10 points below baseline and WORKPLACES turns negative, retail restrictions are typically active. This regime persists over the next two weeks, keeping RETAIL_REC suppressed.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT below -10.0 AND WORKPLACES below 0.0 simultaneously
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT at -11.1, WORKPLACES at -1.7 in t-0w
failure_condition: Either TRANSIT rebounds above -9.0 or WORKPLACES rises above +1.0 within one week, or RETAIL_REC rises above -11.0 despite both conditions remaining met.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility is at its lowest point (-41.3 to -43.1 in recent weeks), indicating a severe constraint on outdoor recreation. This constraint is a leading indicator of broader mobility restrictions that will suppress RETAIL_REC over the next one week as restrictions tighten further.
candidate_trigger: PARKS falls below -40.0 for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS at -43.1 in t-1w and -41.3 in t-0w
failure_condition: PARKS rebounds above -35.0 within one week, or RETAIL_REC rises above -13.0 despite PARKS remaining below -40.0.

mechanism_narrative: The stable negative RETAIL_REC (-13.3 to -13.9) combined with stable elevated RESIDENTIAL (+7.3 to +7.9) and stable elevated GROCERY_PHARM (+9.6 to +10.4) indicates a locked-in behavioral equilibrium: consumers have shifted to home-centric consumption with essential-only outings. This equilibrium is self-reinforcing and will persist over the next four weeks unless a major shock disrupts it.
evidence_refs: fact:All three series show minimal week-to-week variance over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above -11.0 while both RESIDENTIAL remains above +7.0 and GROCERY_PHARM remains above +9.0, or any series shows a variance increase exceeding 2.0 points week-on-week.
